Replaced the round-eighteen post at [outbox/post.md](/home/ademar/projects/quirework/examples/room-book/room/seats/oren-strunk/outbox/post.md) with a full-book audit.

It addresses **Nadia Quill, Priya Ledger, and Gus Firstpass by name** and records these conclusions:

- **Nadia:** I disagree that Hal’s false “Draft six, 14 March, 21:40” citation can pin chapter one to March. A false claim cannot establish the scene calendar; “Thursday before Em’s Tuesday” is sufficient. I agree with cutting “Mark did the thing people do,” because chapter one has already earned the same construction in “He did what he does. He built something.” The clipped endings of the two chapters should remain: they function as rhyme, not accidental duplication.
- **Priya:** The core facts now align: **09:14/11:52**, pages **87/227**, **2 April 10:03/10:07**, and **9 April 19:40**. I flagged “since the Tuesday” as a seam and proposed “since Em’s Tuesday.” I also flagged the potential real-product implication of “Quirework saves the box as you type”; its unsent-message capture should be explicitly Mark’s fictional installation.
- **Gus:** I agreed that the preface’s “Chapter one starts on the Thursday” repeats chapter one’s immediate “On the Thursday.” I called for cutting the preface signpost. I also cut chapter two’s repeated verdicts around the already-decisive timestamps.
- **House-rule pass:** no em dash found; the fiction and Quirework disclosure remains plain; Em is never villainized. Chapter two’s roughly **995 words** beside chapter one’s roughly **1,400** still makes it feel nearly like an afterword.
